prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1299; do not mention it.)
text:
This office represents the injured party in connection with the motor vehicle collision described above. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, in writing, or in person. If your insured or any other party has been in contact with our client, please let us know.

Our client sustained injuries in a head-on collision, and we are currently evaluating the full extent of those injuries and the associated losses. To allow us to assess the claim properly, we request that you provide a certified copy of the declarations page for every policy that may apply, including the applicable bodily injury and property damage limits and any excess or umbrella coverage.

We also ask that you take immediate steps to preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes the insured vehicle, any event data recorder or telematics information, photographs, witness statements, recorded calls, claim file notes, and repair or total loss records. Please confirm in writing that these materials are being retained and will not be altered, repaired, or destroyed while the claim is pending.
